articles.title: Singapore's Energy Capital Global to invest ₹41,750 crore in AI -Ready Data Centre campus ...
articles.content: Chhattisgarh took a major step towards becoming a hub for India’s digital economy today, securing foreign direct investment (FDI) commitments worth ₹43,250 crore at the inaugural Singapore-India Network for Growth (SING) Forum 2026 in Singapore. The commitments included a single ₹41,750-crore investment for an AI-ready data centre campus. Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai led the State delegation at the Forum, where Chhattisgarh participated on the nomination of the Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India. Advertisement The landmark commitment comes from Singapore-headquartered Energy Capital Global Pte Ltd, which will establish a 100-MW AI-ready data centre campus in Chhattisgarh. Advertisement Energy Capital Global develops and finances AI-ready data centres paired with on-site clean power across the Asia-Pacific region, with a presence in Singapore, India, Malaysia, Kazakhstan and Australia. The Chief Minister handed over the Invitation to Invest to the company at the Forum. The commitment builds on Chhattisgarh’s growing digital momentum, as the State is already home to India’s first AI Data Centre Park. Together, these projects are positioning Chhattisgarh as a rising hub for India’s digital infrastructure. “Chhattisgarh has the power, the land and the political will that AI infrastructure needs, and it has them today. This MoU is the start of a long-term partnership. We look forward to building the largest AI-ready data centre campus in central India, bringing international capital and expertise to the State, and training Chhattisgarh’s engineers to run it,” said Stanislav Borisov, Chief Executive Officer, Energy Capital Global. The State also received an FDI commitment of ₹1,500 crore from Sunstream Green Energy Pvt Ltd in the solar sector, along with investments in related battery storage and components. Chief Minister Sai said that these commitments were a vote of confidence in Chhattisgarh’s policies, potential and people. He added that they would create new opportunities for the State’s youth and bring Chhattisgarh closer to its goal of a Viksit Chhattisgarh. The Chief Minister also took part in a fireside chat alongside Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, moderated by the Singapore Business Federation. Making a compelling case for Chhattisgarh, he said, “We don’t bring reforms by discussing them in closed rooms. We ask industry directly about their difficulties and change our systems to match. Over 450 reforms have been completed, and this Reform Express will not stop until people themselves say no more reform is needed.” He added that this combination of reforms, a progressive industrial policy and a proactive government had brought Chhattisgarh investment proposals worth over ₹8 lakh crore in just 18 months. Gan Siow Huang, Minister of State, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Trade and Industry, Government of Singapore, graced the Forum as the Guest of Honour. Her presence underlined the importance Singapore places on deepening economic ties with Indian States. Senior leadership from global corporations, including Mastercard, IHCL (Taj Hotels) and Nestlé, also addressed the gathering. On the sidelines of the Forum, the Chief Minister held one-on-one meetings with Aquatech and Adroit Overseas Pte Ltd. The discussions focused on wastewater reuse...

articles.title: Beyond Battery Monitoring: Building the Intelligence Layer for India's Connected EV Fleets
articles.content: The rapid scaling of commercial electric vehicle (EV) fleets is driving a fundamental shift in mobility management, moving from simple asset tracking to AI-powered predictive intelligence. As high-value battery packs dictate total cost of ownership, fleet availability, and operational lifespan, enterprises can no longer rely on basic telematics that merely report isolated metrics. By processing real-time IoT streams alongside historical performance, driver behavior, and charging patterns, organizations can contextualize complex sensor data, transform emergency repairs into proactive maintenance, and maximize vehicle uptime across demanding operational environments. Unlocking the full value of fleet electrification requires bridging fragmented data streams across diverse vehicles, battery chemistries, and charging infrastructure into a unified intelligence layer. As EVs increasingly integrate with broader energy ecosystems, technology solutions must remain flexible, interoperable, and focused on solving clear operational challenges—ensuring that data insights directly translate into extended asset lifecycles, lower maintenance costs, and improved total cost of ownership. “The larger trend is towards making EV assets increasingly intelligent, connected and measurable throughout their lifecycle,” said Abhinav Bhargava, CTO & Co-founder at Ursaa Energyworx. How is AI changing the way enterprises manage connected vehicles and EV fleets today? Abhinav: AI is assisting businesses in transforming from just gathering vehicle and battery information to utilizing it in practice. At Ursaa, we have seen this evolution firsthand. Our active connected-asset base grew from 5,000 assets in September 2023 to 20,000 by July 2024. Today, Ursaa has expanded to 43,000+ connected assets across five countries, giving us exposure to diverse real-world operating environments. By monitoring data generated by vehicles, batteries, telematics, and operational conditions, connected electric vehicle fleets can analyze this information for trends affecting factors such as performance, energy usage, battery condition, and maintenance. This is a major change from merely responding to issues in fleet management to decision-making that is driven by forecasted outcomes. AI and machine learning offer insight into when operational components or batteries might fail. What is driving the shift from basic battery monitoring to predictive battery intelligence? Abhinav: The monitoring process provides information about the performance of the battery at any particular moment. Predictive battery intelligence improves the monitoring process by providing additional insights about the reasons behind certain events as well as possible developments. With the growth of electric vehicle deployments, companies obtain more and more data regarding batteries. The data can be analyzed with the goal of identifying factors that may force the battery to malfunction. The transformation of the monitoring process is crucial as the batteries’ condition has a significant impact on vehicles’ availability, economy, and lifecycle management. How can predictive analytics help EV fleets reduce battery-related downtime and improve operational efficiency? Abhinav: Predictive analytics is one powerful resource to see any changes that can arise in batteries well before they lead to potential problems in their operations. By continuously checking the historical data from the vehicle and battery, fleet managers will detect the patterns suggesting battery degradation and abnormal performance. articles.title: NYAI AI Studio Unifies AI Agents, Data and Legal Workflows - SMEStreet
articles.content: Technology For SMEs IoT & AI NYAI AI Studio Unifies AI Agents, Data and Legal Workflows NYAI launches AI Studio, an agentic AI infrastructure platform for law firms and enterprises, integrating AI agents, workflows, data and governance in one platform. SMEStreet Edit Desk 05 Oct 2026 13:22 IST Follow Us New Update Listen to this article 0.75x 1x 1.5x 00:00 / 00:00 NYAI, the legal and compliance AI company, launched NYAI AI Studio, India’s first agentic AI infrastructure platform purpose-built for law firms and the legal and compliance functions of enterprises. The Studio marks a decisive shift from AI that assists with discrete tasks to AI agents that execute legal and compliance work end to end, from intake to delivery, on the organisation’s own data, under its own controls and through its own choice of AI models. Rather than adding yet another point solution to an already crowded legal-technology stack, NYAI AI Studio unites data, agents, models, tools, workflows, institutional knowledge and governance within a single environment, giving every organisation the infrastructure to build an AI practice in its own image. “Legal and compliance teams cannot treat AI as merely another productivity application. Their work turns on sensitive client information, proprietary institutional knowledge, intricate processes and decisions that demand complete traceability. Above all, one size does not fit all in legal and compliance. Every firm has its own playbooks, every enterprise its own regulatory footprint, and every matter its own contours. A generic AI tool cannot do justice to that diversity. NYAI AI Studio was, therefore, the need of the hour: a platform on which each organisation builds precisely the agents and workflows its practice demands.” Advocate Dr. Chinmay S. Bhosale, Co-founder, NYAI From AI Applications to AI Infrastructure The rapid adoption of generative AI has created a new governance problem for legal and compliance organisations. Sensitive data is increasingly dispersed across multiple AI applications, often with scant visibility into what information is processed, by which model, by whom and at what cost. NYAI AI Studio resolves this by operating as the infrastructure layer beneath those applications. It is model-agnostic by design, integrating with Claude, GPT, Microsoft Copilot and Gemini, while organisational data remains within the NYAI environment and inference runs through the AI ecosystem each organisation selects. Teams may thus deploy the right model for each task rather than depending on a single model for every use case. Tailored for Every Organisation The Studio pairs ready-to-deploy agents for everyday legal work with a builder that enables lawyers and compliance professionals, not merely engineers, to design their own. Organisations can encode their playbooks, precedents, clause libraries and escalation protocols into bespoke agents, tools, skills and workflows, rather than conforming their practice to the fixed functionality of packaged software. A knowledge graph and organisational memory retain matter-level and institutional context, so that each engagement enriches the next and an organisation’s collective expertise compounds over time. articles.title: India Demonstrates First Free- Space Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) Link - INSIGHTS IAS
articles.content: Subject: Science and Technology Context: QNu Labs, BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar demonstrated India’s first free-space Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) link , securely transmitting quantum keys over 5.56 km. Quantum Key Distribution About India Demonstrates First Free-Space Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) Link : What it is? A state-of-the-art secure communication technology that uses the fundamental principles of quantum mechanics to transmit cryptographic encryption keys through unguided optical channels in open air (free space), rather than through fiber-optic cables. Organisations Involved: QNu Labs: Bengaluru-based deep-tech startup developing indigenous quantum-secure hardware, including Armos QKD and PAT systems . BISAG-N: MeitY autonomous scientific society that integrated its post-quantum cryptography platform, Vedic Kavach. IIT Gandhinagar: Academic partner providing the testing environment through its Interdisciplinary School of Technology and Future (ISTF). Aim: To build sovereign, tamper-proof communication infrastructure resilient against quantum decryption threats, laying the technical foundation for satellite-to-ground quantum communications and secure defense networks . How It Works? Single-Photon Key Encoding: Cryptographic keys are encoded onto individual photons generated by QNu Labs’ Armos hardware device. Line-of-Sight Laser Transmission: An active Pointing, Acquisition, and Tracking (PAT) optical terminal aligns the transmitter and receiver across the 5.56-km open-air path, compensating in real time for atmospheric turbulence, and minor structural vibrations. Eavesdropping Detection via Quantum Physics : Governed by the Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle and the No-Cloning Theorem , any third-party attempt to intercept or measure the photons alters their quantum states, immediately introducing detectable errors. Key Sifting & Dual-Layer Encryption : If the Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) stays within acceptable thresholds (<5%), the raw quantum bits are distilled into shared symmetric keys and fed into the Vedic Kavach post-quantum cryptographic software layer for final message encryption. Key Features: Line-of-Sight Free-Space Range: Successfully bridged a 5.56-km atmospheric distance through open air without physical fiber infrastructure, proving viable in dense urban and suburban topographies. Low Error Rate & Key Generation Speed: Maintained a stable QBER below 5% while continuously generating secure symmetric keys at an operational rate of 230 to 260 bits per second (bps). Dual-Layer Defense-in-Depth Architecture: Combines hardware-level quantum physics with mathematical post-quantum cryptography ensuring uninterrupted operational encryption even during temporary optical channel outages. Advanced Optical Alignment (PAT): Incorporates high-precision Pointing, Acquisition, and Tracking optical sub-systems essential for maintaining narrow laser collimation across open-air atmospheric turbulence. Triple-Helix Innovation Model: Represents a successful collaborative integration of academic research (IIT Gandhinagar), private deep-tech enterprise (QNu Labs), and government R&D institutions (BISAG-N/MeitY). Applications: Space Communications: Supports future satellite-to-ground and inter-satellite quantum networks for secure key transmission. Defence Communications: Enables secure, deployable line-of-sight links for military, naval and mobile field operations. Critical Infrastructure : Protects sensitive intelligence, nuclear and space communications against future quantum-enabled cyber threats. Difficult Terrains: Enables secure connectivity across rivers, valleys and disaster-hit areas where laying fibre is impractical.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh to Pilot India's First 3D-Printed Rural Houses under PMAY-G
articles.content: Subject: Miscellaneous Context: Andhra Pradesh is set to launch India’s first national-level pilot project to construct rural houses using 3D Concrete Printing (3DCP) under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G) scheme. Andhra Pradesh to Pilot India’s First 3D-Printed Rural Houses under PMAY-G About Andhra Pradesh to Pilot India’s First 3D-Printed Rural Houses under PMAY-G : What is 3D Concrete Printing (3DCP) ? An automated, construction-scale additive manufacturing technology that replaces traditional manual brick-and-mortar masonry by depositing high-performance cementitious mixtures layer-by-layer using robotic gantry or arm printers. How it works? Digital Modeling: A 3D architectural plan is created using Building Information Modelling (BIM) and sliced into precise numerical computer paths . Material Extrusion: A computer-guided robotic nozzle extrudes specially engineered fluid concrete mix along the toolpath. Rapid In-Situ Setting : The extruded concrete formulation maintains high buildability and fast setting properties to rapidly form load-bearing walls and enclosures without conventional formwork. Key Features: High Construction Speed & Automation: Compresses traditional structural wall construction timelines from several months down to just a few days or hours, drastically cutting reliance on sequential manual labour. Material Optimization & Zero Formwork Waste : Uses precise digital deposition without requiring conventional wooden or steel scaffolding/molds, reducing raw material usage and job-site construction waste by up to 30–60%. Architectural & Design Flexibility: Seamlessly prints complex structural geometries, curved walls, and customized thermal or acoustic cavity designs without escalating tooling costs. High Structural Durability: Produces uniform, dense, and seismically compliant concrete envelopes with engineered structural strength and lower long-term maintenance burdens. About the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G) Scheme : What it is? The flagship rural social-welfare housing programme of the Government of India, implemented to provide financial assistance to homeless and vulnerable rural households to build durable pucca houses with basic amenities. Established in: Restructured from the erstwhile Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY) and officially launched on November 20, 2016 (effective from April 1, 2016) by Prime Minister Narendra Modi under the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD). Aim: To fulfill the mandate of Housing for All across rural India by providing safe, secure, disaster-resilient, and hygienic homes equipped with clean cooking spaces, electricity, and sanitation facilities. Key Features: Unit Assistance & Cost-Sharing: Provides direct financial grants of ₹1.20 lakh per unit in plain areas (shared 60:40 between Centre and States) and ₹1.30 lakh in North-Eastern, Himalayan states, and difficult/UT areas (shared 90:10 or 100% Central). Mandated Minimum Space & Design Standards : Sets a minimum carpet area of 25 sq. metres (including a dedicated hygienic cooking space ), with disaster-resilient typologies tailored to local geographical and climatic conditions. Objective Beneficiary Identification : Selects beneficiaries using housing deficiency parameters from the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 and Awaas+ mobile surveys, subject to mandatory verification by Gram Sabhas. Cross-Scheme Convergence: Automatically links beneficiaries to MGNREGA, Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin, Jal Jeevan Mission, and PM Ujjwala Yojana.

articles.title: VOC Port in Thoothukudi to set up India's first offshore wind turbine - DT Next
articles.content: CHENNAI : The VO Chidambaranar Port Authority in Thoothukudi will install a 6.25 MW wind turbine in sea and transmit the electricity generated to the State grid, in a Rs 77.41-crore project that would serve as India's first offshore wind-farm prototype. The project, which involves installing a turbine on a foundation built on the seabed and laying a submarine cable to bring the power to the shore, is scheduled for completion within 12 months of the Letter of Acceptance. Unlike conventional wind farms with multiple turbines, the proposed installation will have only one turbine; but the project will build experience in offshore installation, marine logistics, and grid connectivity. The turbine will be located about 1.65 km from the southern breakwater of the existing Inner Harbour and around 1 km from the proposed southern breakwater of the Outer Harbour. The seabed at the site is about 9.7 metres below Chart Datum, the reference level used to measure water depth. The contractor will have to conduct site-specific seabed and marine surveys before designing the foundation and installing the turbine. The work also includes supplying the vessels and lifting equipment required for offshore installation, laying the submarine export cable, and providing the associated electrical and control systems. The cable must be buried or otherwise protected as required. Electricity generated by the turbine will be stepped up to 22 kV through a transformer and carried by the subsea cable to a Transition Joint Bay at the port's existing substation. From there, the power will be connected to the State grid. Onshore meters will record electricity exported to and imported from the grid in accordance with Tangedco and Tantransco norms. The sequence includes detailed surveys and engineering, equipment procurement, foundation installation, cable laying, turbine installation, and electrical integration, followed by testing and commissioning. The contractor will also be responsible for the required environmental studies and statutory approvals. The turbine will have three blades mounted on a tubular steel tower, with a minimum design life of 25 years. The contract, issued by Indian Port Rail - Ropeway Corporation Ltd (IPRCL) on behalf of the port, includes two years of operation and maintenance after commissioning. After commissioning, the turbine must meet specified performance requirements, including at least 95% annual machine availability, an energy-production demonstration test and a 96-hour reliability run without faults or alarms. India has pursued offshore wind development off Tamil Nadu and Gujarat coasts for more than a decade, but the sector has yet to take off.

articles.title: Claude Goes Live in India with In-Country Inference Through Amazon Bedrock - CXO Today
articles.content: Anthropic today announced that Claude models — including Claude Opus 5, Sonnet 5, and Haiku 4.5 — are now live with in-country inference in India through Amazon Bedrock . Requests sent to Claude through the India endpoint are now processed within India, giving regulated Indian institutions the data residency assurances they need to deploy Claude at scale across their most sensitive workloads. Source: Anthropic India is one of the largest markets for Claude globally and home to one of the most technically sophisticated developer communities Anthropic serves. A recurring request from Indian organizations has been the ability to run inference locally — a requirement that is often an imperative for financial institutions, government bodies and large enterprises operating under strict regulatory and data-handling standards. That capability is now available. “In August, we committed to bringing Claude inference to India, and we are delivering on that promise. Our customers, especially in regulated sectors and government, want to use Claude on their most critical work, with requests processed in the country. From today, they can,” said Irina Ghose, Managing Director, India, Anthropic. “This is a long-term commitment. We will keep growing our team in India and investing in local partnerships.” Sandeep Dutta, President, AWS India and South Asia, said: “Responsible AI adoption at scale has become a strategic imperative for some of India’s most regulated industries. For them, data residency is the parameter that decides whether AI stays confined to pilots or reaches full production. With in-country inference for Claude now available through Amazon Bedrock, requests are processed on servers based in India, enabling banks, insurers, and public institutions to trust and deploy AI at a production scale.” Claude deployments through Amazon Bedrock in India come with the audit trails and access controls that risk and compliance teams require before deploying AI in production environments. Early customers including Reliance, CRED, and others tested in private preview. Customers across industries welcomed the launch. Some pointed to the lower latency, performance, resilience and others to the regulatory alignment of running Claude locally and the need to keep data within Indian borders. Here is what customers across industries had to say. “As Anthropic’s customer and partner in India, we are pleased with this announcement. Local inference gives us the performance, resilience and regulatory alignment we need to move Claude into production areas across the Reliance ecosystem.”—Reliance Industries. “As Anthropic’s Global Premier Partner, with one of the world’s largest pools of Claude certified talent, we see growing demand for enterprise-grade AI deployments in regulated industries. Anthropic’s in-country inference capability in India is an important step in meeting evolving data residency and governance requirements. Together, we are helping enterprises accelerate their journey.” – Amit Kapur, Chief AI & Services Transformation Officer, TCS. “In-country inference widens the options available to Indian banks. At Kotak, we built a single AI platform with governance designed in from the start, which lets us adopt new capabilities like this responsibly and at pace.” – Vijay Narayanan, Head of Innovation & AI, Kotak...

articles.title: Assam to Get India's First Underwater Road-cum-Rail Tunnel - RAHSTA Expo
articles.content: Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari has announced that Assam will host India’s first and the world’s second underwater road-cum-rail twin-tube tunnel. The project will run beneath the Brahmaputra, linking Gohpur with Numaligarh and creating a shorter route between the two locations. Gadkari said the development would improve connectivity across Assam and neighbouring north-eastern states. Gadkari said the required approvals for the project had been obtained and indicated that construction could begin before the end of December, subject to the planned foundation ceremony. The approved project has a total capital cost of Rs. 220 bn. No completion date has been announced for the corridor or tunnel. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the project in February. It comprises a 33.7-km four-lane, access-controlled corridor between Gohpur on NH-15 and Numaligarh on NH-715. Its central component is a 15.79-km twin-tube tunnel beneath the Brahmaputra, with one tube incorporating railway infrastructure. Once operational, the corridor will connect two airports, four railway stations and two inland waterways. It will also link 11 economic nodes, three social nodes and two tourist nodes. The listed tourist destinations are Kaziranga National Park and the Deopahar Archaeological Site. The existing road distance between Gohpur and Numaligarh is about 240 km, and the journey currently takes around six hours. The new corridor is projected to reduce the travel time to about 20 minutes. It is also expected to improve links with Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and other parts of the Northeast, while supporting freight movement, lowering logistics costs and encouraging regional economic activity.

articles.title: India's First Agentic AI Campus Takes Shape at KLH Hyderabad - CXO Today
articles.content: KLH Hyderabad today inaugurated its Agentic AI Campus initiative and signed an MoU with HCL Group AI Labs, unveiling a roadmap that places AI-powered learning and student innovation at the centre of its academic vision. The collaboration aims to equip students across disciplines to understand, build and apply intelligent technologies through practical projects, faculty mentorship and industry engagement. Mr. Deepak Sarvanan, National Head, HCL Group AI Labs, formally inaugurated the initiative at a press meet in KLH Bachupally campus in Hyderabad. Dr. L. Koteswara Rao, Principal, KLH Bachupally, represented KLH at the MoU exchange, alongside Dr. A. Srinath, Dean – Skill Development, in the presence of other senior officials, deans, faculty and staff. The initiative aims to make AI an integral part of the student experience. From exploring concepts in the classroom to developing applications, students will be encouraged to use AI to investigate problems, test ideas and create solutions relevant to industry and society. Er. Koneru Lakshman Havish, Vice President, KL Deemed to be University said, “We want students to develop the confidence and skills to shape how AI is used in their chosen fields. Our collaboration with HCL Group AI Labs will help connect classroom learning with hands-on projects and industry expertise, giving students opportunities to build intelligent solutions for real-world needs. As we develop our Agentic AI Campus, our focus is on preparing young people to innovate responsibly and contribute meaningfully to an evolving workplace.” Agentic AI brings a new dimension to this approach. These systems can plan and carry out a series of tasks towards a defined goal, with appropriate human oversight. Understanding how such systems work will help students explore applications that extend from analysing information to coordinating workflows and supporting decisions. The proposed roadmap envisages project-based learning in areas such as business automation, data-driven services and discipline-specific AI applications. Students will be encouraged to design and test solutions, evaluating their accuracy, reliability and practical value. Faculty readiness will be a key part of the campus’s development. The collaboration envisages supporting educators in integrating AI into teaching, assignments and mentorship, helping students connect technical understanding with critical thinking and independent judgement. Responsible AI use will remain central to the learning approach, with attention to data privacy, bias, reliability and human accountability. Students will be encouraged to question outputs, verify information and understand the limitations of the systems they develop and use. Through its collaboration with HCL Group AI Labs, KLH Hyderabad aims to strengthen the connection between academic learning and the evolving workplace across its Bachupally and Aziznagar campuses, preparing students to develop AI solutions and apply them thoughtfully to real-world challenges.

articles.title: AMD samples space -grade Versal AI Core processing chip. - Bisinfotech
articles.content: Image Credits: AMD There has been a move within the space industry in terms of conducting advanced level analytics directly on the satellites and not just transmitting the sensor data to Earth because of limited bandwidth and the long period of delay in deep-space transmissions. With such challenges, there is a requirement to analyze images, radar data, and other sensors in real time. To cater to this growing need, AMD has begun sampling its latest space-grade version of Versal AI Core processing chip. High-Reliability Packaging Built for Extreme Flight Conditions Space hardware needs to be capable of surviving extreme temperatures changes, stresses caused during the launch process, as well as radiation for a period of time which can extend for up to 15 years. The conventional technology used in making space chips is based on ceramics which are heavy and sealed according to MIL-PRF-38535 Class V. This packaging suffers from several physical limitations. To overcome these constraints, the new space-grade Versal processing platform uses an advanced non-hermetic, lidless organic package. Key design features include: Direct Die Heat Spreading: The removal of the lid results in direct exposure of the silicon die to the cooling system of the satellite, thus reducing thermal resistance and ensuring stability of the chip in the vacuum environment. Improved Materials: The assembly incorporates the improved organic substrate along with the space-qualified capacitors with flight heritage. Compatibility of Design: The chip is designed with the industry-standard 2197 ball-grid array package and allows using the same PCB layouts as were used for early commercial prototypes up to the flight model. High-Density Onboard Compute for Autonomous Missions Modern space payload applications use a lot of vector operations, machine learning, sensor fusion, and radar processing. The mixed architecture of this adaptive platform includes general programmable logic, distributed memory, high-speed transceivers, and vector processing units in one piece of hardware. This eliminates the need for control from the ground station and makes satellite downlinks more efficient. Space Qualification and Industry Standards To fill in the gap between commercial speed and reliability of spaceflight, standards organizations like NASA and JEDEC have introduced MIL-PRF-38535 Class Y certification. Class Y requires highly rigorous manufacturing, screening, and testing procedures for advanced non-hermetically packaged organic substrate packages for use in critical missions of space applications. articles.title: TDB Signs ₹130 Crore Deal for AI Vision SoC - GKToday
articles.content: Home TDB Signs ₹130 Crore Deal for AI Vision SoC TDB Signs ₹130 Crore Deal for AI Vision SoC October 5, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 The Technology Development Board (TDB) under the Department of Science & Technology signed an agreement with Bengaluru-based BigEndian Semiconductors on 5 October 2026 for Project VeerAI. The agreement provides ₹130 crore under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund for the development of an indigenous AI Vision System-on-Chip (SoC). Technology Development Board and RDI Fund The Technology Development Board was established under the Technology Development Board Act, 1995, and functions under the Department of Science & Technology. The RDI Fund is used for supporting research, development, and innovation projects in strategic and emerging technology areas. Project VeerAI and System-on-Chip Project VeerAI has a total project cost of ₹260 crore, and TDB’s support is structured as Optional Convertible Debt (OCD). A System-on-Chip integrates multiple electronic components, such as processors, memory, and input-output interfaces, on a single semiconductor chip. AI Vision SoC and Technology Readiness Level The project aims to develop a camera-focused AI Vision SoC on a sovereign technology platform. The stated objective is to move the product from Technology Readiness Level 5 to Technology Readiness Level 9, where TRL-5 refers to validation in a relevant environment and TRL-9 refers to an actual system proven in operational use. Important Facts for Exams The Technology Development Board operates under the Department of Science & Technology, which is a ministry-level department of the Government of India. Optional Convertible Debt is a financing instrument that can be converted into equity under specified conditions. System-on-Chip technology is widely used in smartphones, surveillance systems, automotive electronics, and industrial devices. Technology Readiness Level is a nine-point scale used to assess the maturity of a technology from concept to deployment. Applications and Strategic Use The indigenous AI Vision SoC is intended for secure AI chips used in CCTV-based surveillance systems. The platform is also planned for defence, automotive, industrial, and medical applications, with an emphasis on reducing dependence on external semiconductor supply chains. Semiconductor Ecosystem in India India has been expanding its semiconductor design and manufacturing ecosystem through policy support, research funding, and industry partnerships. Bengaluru remains a major centre for semiconductor design, electronics engineering, and deep-tech start-ups in India. articles.title: QNu Labs completes India's first 5-km free- space QKD - Bisinfotech
articles.content: QNu Labs , a global leader in end-to-end hybrid quantum cybersecurity solutions, along with the Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics (BISAG-N), and IIT Gandhinagar, have successfully completed a 5.56 km free-space Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) field trial, marking India’s first free-space QKD link at the 5 km scale. The field trial demonstrates the ability to establish and maintain a quantum-secured communication link over open atmosphere while integrating QKD generated keys with a post-quantum cryptography (PQC) enabled application environment. Conducted on the night of September 27–28, 2026, the trial established a 5.56 km free-space quantum communication link between BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar, with QNu Labs’ Pointing, Acquisition and Tracking (PAT) system maintaining the 1550 nm quantum channel. Using the DPS-Decoy QKD protocol, the link achieved a stable QBER below 5% and a secure key rate of 230–260 bps. The trial also demonstrated the end-to-end integration of QKD with BISAG-N’s Vedic Kavach PQC enabled browser and web server, with 256-bit keys delivered through the ETSI GS QKD 014 interface, enabling a test message to be encrypted, transmitted and successfully decrypted. The trial combined two complementary layers of quantum security. QNu Labs’ QKD technology provided hardware-based quantum key distribution over the free-space optical channel, while Vedic Kavach provided a software layer based on post-quantum cryptography and quantum random number generation (QRNG). The architecture was designed so that the application remains protected even if the physical quantum channel is temporarily unavailable, providing a practical approach to building quantum-resilient communication systems. Sunil Gupta, Co-founder and CEO, QNu Labs, said, “ Quantum security will become meaningful at scale only when technologies can move beyond controlled laboratory environments and operate across real communication infrastructure . This field trial shows that QKD, supported by precise optical pointing and tracking, can be deployed over a multi-kilometre free-space link and integrated with a post-quantum security layer. The successful 5.56 km demonstration is an important step towards developing longer-distance quantum-secure networks and exploring architectures that can eventually support multiple nodes and satellite-based quantum communication.” Qorvo Advances C-Band Radar Front Ends with BAW-Based Frequency Agility and GaN Power Also Read The technical performance of the trial was enabled by QNu Labs’ PAT system, which used coarse pointing through a gimbal and fine steering at a 100 Hz tracking bandwidth to maintain alignment between the two terminals. The system achieved coarse pointing accuracy of 5 microradians and fine pointing accuracy of up to 0.1 microradians, enabling the quantum channel to remain aligned despite atmospheric conditions and physical movement along the optical path. Cmde Manish Tripathi (Retd.), In-charge, ISTF, IIT-G said, “The successful demonstration of a 5.56 km free-space QKD link provides a valuable field environment for advancing practical quantum communication technologies. articles.content: New Delhi (India), October 5, 2026 : Airtel Business, India's leading provider of secure and reliable connectivity, technology, and communications solutions, today launched Airtel IQ Gateway, India’s first ever telco-grade network intelligence platform which brings different customer communication channels onto one safe control plane. Enterprises now won’t need to manage multiple vendors separately if they opt for Airtel IQ Gateway, a DPDP-compliant platform which combines SMS, WhatsApp, RCS, voice communications and number verification (silent authentication) together in one place. It will enable enterprises to easily manage their business communications at scale, while protecting customer trust and making safety foundational to every customer interaction. This offering from Airtel Business is of critical importance today, when businesses have to manage fragmented customer communication stacks across multiple service providers and tools to reach their customers, with limited visibility into the real delivery of messages. Messages are often reported delivered even when they fail, while International OTP pumping by bots inflates bills. Moreover, managing pre-approved message templates is manual and often leads to mistakes. For enterprises, especially in sectors like BFSI, government, e‑commerce and logistics, this not only hurts customer trust when consumers are targeted by scams, this also damages their brand reputation. Airtel IQ Gateway solves this with a single control center for all business communications. It brings together Airtel’s fraud protection with automatic integrations of native message template system (DLT), automatic switching to back-up service providers, and intelligent routing across SMS, WhatsApp, RCS and voice. By leveraging Airtel’s built-in network intelligence and trust layers for enterprise use, such as IQ Verify for fraud protection and Silent Authentication for SIM based login, with capabilities like spotting fraudulent account creations and takeovers and artificial traffic spikes, Airtel IQ Gateway protects enterprises from fraud losses and billing spikes caused by industry-wide SMS pumping. Launched nationwide today after successful trial deployments across select banks, financial institutions and other relevant industry collaborations, the platform extends Airtel’s proven expertise in fraud prevention for end customers to enterprises, enabling them to build customer trust at scale through safe communications. Sharat Sinha, CEO – Airtel Business , said, “As India accelerates towards a safe, inclusive digital economy, trust must become the foundation of every digital interaction. Secure-by-design customer engagement is today the bedrock on which enterprises can scale with confidence. At Airtel, we have already demonstrated the power of network-grade fraud prevention in protecting millions of consumers across our mobile and digital services. With IQ Gateway, we are extending this proven expertise to enterprises, enabling them to build brand trust while ensuring every customer conversation is safe, authenticated and resilient. By embedding trust at the network layer, we are enabling our enterprise customers, especially banks, government departments and logistics firms, to reduce cybercrime losses and strengthen the credibility of every customer interaction. This is a decisive step towards a safer digital future for India, where citizens and businesses can transact and engage with equal confidence. ” Key capabilities of Airtel IQ Gateway For more details on Airtel IQ Gateway, log...

articles.title: Free- Space QKD Trial Marks India's Secure Network Push - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Analysis India’s Free-Space QKD Trial Opens a New Secure Networks Path Analysis India’s Free-Space QKD Trial Opens a New Secure Networks Path By Urban Acres October 5, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp India’s first free-space quantum key distribution demonstration over 5.56 km has placed a specialised communications trial at the centre of a larger infrastructure question: how can institutions build secure networks for an era in which conventional protection systems face emerging quantum-era threats? Conducted by QNu Labs with the Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics, or BISAG-N, and IIT-Gn, the field trial established a secure quantum communication channel between the two institutions. The trial took place on the night of September 27–28, according to a Press Information Bureau release cited by the Times of India. It achieved a Quantum Bit Error Rate below 5 per cent and generated secure keys at a rate of 230–260 bits per second. The demonstration used QNu Labs’ Pointing, Acquisition and Tracking system, known as PAT, to support the free-space link. The immediate achievement is technical, but its importance extends beyond the distance covered. A free-space link does not rely on a conventional physical cable between the communicating points. In this demonstration, the connection was established between BISAG-N and IIT-Gn, making the trial a field-based test of quantum-secure communication infrastructure rather than a laboratory exercise alone. The supplied information does not establish that the system has entered routine public or commercial operation. It does, however, identify the trial as a foundation for further development of India’s secure communications capabilities. Quantum key distribution, or QKD, is a method for creating secure encryption keys through quantum communication. In practical terms, the key generated through the process can be used to protect information exchanged between connected parties. The reported performance measures are therefore central to understanding the demonstration: the QBER indicates the level of error recorded in the quantum transmission, while the key rate indicates how quickly secure keys were generated during the trial. The reported QBER of under 5 per cent and key generation rate of 230–260 bps provide a defined technical account of what the trial achieved. They also show why such a demonstration should be read as an infrastructure milestone rather than as evidence of a complete secure communications network. A link can prove that a technology works across a specific distance and setting without establishing how it would perform across a larger network, under changing environmental conditions, or at the scale required by multiple users. None of those wider deployment questions is answered in the supplied material. The trial also combined two layers of quantum security, officials said. The source does not specify the design of those layers or explain how they were integrated, so the significance of the arrangement must be understood within the limits of the available information. What is clear is that the demonstration was designed around more than a single security mechanism and that the participating institutions presented it as a step towards...

articles.title: India demonstrates first free- space quantum link - Nagaland Post
articles.content: National News India demonstrates first free-space quantum link India demonstrates first free-space quantum link October 5, 2026 NEW DELHI, OCT 4 (AGENCIES): Indian deep-tech startup QNu Labs, in collaboration with BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar, has successfully demonstrated India’s first free-space quantum key distribution (QKD) link over 5.56 km. The field trial, conducted on the night of September 27-28, established a secure quantum communication channel between BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar, the IT and electronics ministry said. Using QNu Labs’ pointing, acquisition and tracking system, the trial achieved a stable quantum bit error rate below 5% and generated secure keys at 230-260 bps. The keys were integrated with BISAG-N’s post-quantum cryptography-enabled Vedic Kavach platform, enabling end-to-end encryption and decryption of test messages. BISAG-N director general Vinay Thakur said the integration marked a significant step towards practical quantum-resilient communication systems. QNu Labs co-founder and CEO Sunil Gupta said the demonstration paved the way for longer-distance quantum-secure networks and satellite-based quantum communication. IIT Gandhinagar’s Cmde Manish Tripathi (Retd.) said the trial provided a valuable field environment for advancing practical quantum communication technologies and secure communication infrastructure in India.
